clue.text: Wanted a seat?

parts.note: read literally, someone who wanted a seat had none and was on their feet; a candidate who wanted a seat in Parliament also put themselves up for election

explanation.surface: A simple question about whether someone was looking for somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of the past tense meet: remained on your feet for want of a chair, and offered yourself as a candidate for a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a chair you remained upright on your feet, and a would-be MP put up for a constituency.

clue.text: Don't give in and buy a lot of drinks (about a gallon)

indicators.note: about means the drinks phrase goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to stand one's round is to buy drinks for everyone in a group at the pub

explanation.surface: Refusing to back down while generously paying for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs groups buy drinks in turn, each person standing a round. 'a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold firm and refuse to retreat or yield.

clue.text: Birdie last two at Birkdale, coming in two up

indicators.note: coming in says those letters go inside the other piece
in a down entry up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last two at picks the final pair of letters of the golf course's name

explanation.surface: A golfer scoring a birdie on the closing holes at a links, going two up.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Birkdale is an English links golf course; in golf a birdie is one under par, but here it means a little bird. 'up' turns the number over in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is a baby bird, and birdie is a childish word for a little bird.

clue.text: Let loose and used abusive language when upset

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: reviled means attacked with insults

explanation.surface: Someone who swore furiously when angry and then released it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suggests anger or an anagram, but in a down entry it turns REVILED over.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free or release, as in rescuing someone from danger.

clue.text: Lab worker shows, after medicine, one's temperature is greatly reduced

indicators.note: after says the piece for one's follows the medicine word in the answer

parts.note: physic is an old word for medicine or a medicinal draught
one is I, and one's is read as one is, giving I plus S

indicators.note: the word temperature cut down drastically to just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A report that a lab worker, after taking medicine, has a much lower fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' and 'is' are link words. 'greatly reduced' shrinks 'temperature' to its first letter T, the usual abbreviation anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies matter and energy typically works in a laboratory.

clue.text: Choose the best tool

definitions.meaning: the ... of the bunch is the finest

explanation.surface: A craftsman selecting the finest implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Three meanings: select, the choicest of a group, and a pointed tool for breaking ground.

clue.text: Rare, yes, yet possibly found in the past

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unusual items perhaps turning up from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary word for times gone by, as in the snows of long ago.

clue.text: Gather round American tea-maker

indicators.note: round says the deduction word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: to gather can mean to conclude or deduce

explanation.surface: People assembling around a US-made teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like assembling, but it is the sense of concluding.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that holds leaves steeping in hot water to brew a drink.

clue.text: Absorption in baptism

definitions.meaning: complete absorption in an activity or subject
baptism by full submersion in water

explanation.surface: Being wholly engrossed in a religious rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep engagement in something, and dipping a person wholly under water at a christening.

clue.text: Give up and add dryer at no extra cost

definitions.meaning: to concede defeat, from a boxer's corner throwing in a towel

definitions.text: add dryer at no extra cost
definitions.meaning: to throw in is to include free, and a towel dries you

explanation.surface: A shop surrendering and giving away a free bath sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means surrender; read literally it means including a drying cloth free of charge.

clue.text: To score 147, you need these top sportsmen

definitions.meaning: a maximum break of 147 in snooker means potting the black after every red, fifteen times, then all the colours
the New Zealand national rugby union team, among the best in the world

explanation.surface: Advice on what it takes to reach a perfect score, praising elite athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue game played mainly in Britain; its maximum break of 147 needs fifteen blacks. The New Zealand rugby side wear all-black kit and are named for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a snooker player's sequence of black-ball pots and the famous New Zealand rugby team, known for their dark kit.

clue.text: Skin covers me over

indicators.note: covers means the skin word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: fur is an animal's skin or pelt

indicators.note: over signals that the word me is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bone speaking of itself: flesh and skin lie on top of me.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the thigh bone, which skin covers, while 'covers' and 'over' also do the mechanical work.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is buried in the leg, sheathed by muscle and skin.

clue.text: Show diamonds around in this case

indicators.note: around signals the musical's name turned round end to end

parts.note: Evita is a stage musical, a West End show
D is the card abbreviation for the suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: An instruction to display some gems set around a particular example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the whole of EVITA plus D backwards. 'in this' is linking; 'Show' looks like a verb but names the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical case in Latin, German and other languages, marking the indirect object.

clue.text: Plant put in part of garden by sucker

indicators.note: by means the second piece is placed beside the first

parts.note: a flower bed is a part of a garden
a drinking straw is something you suck through

explanation.surface: A gardener putting a plant in a border next to a sucker shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' suggests a horticultural shoot, but it is something you suck a drink through. 'put in' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild herb of the genus Galium, once used to stuff mattresses.

clue.text: Style of art once fashionable, type one introduced

indicators.note: introduced means the category word goes into the middle of the rearranged letters
fashionable here means fashioned anew, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
a class is a type or category
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A movement in art that used to be trendy, with one new kind brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' says the letters are fashioned anew, and 'introduced' sets the category word into the middle of them. 'once fashionable' looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival of the forms of ancient Greek and Roman art.

clue.text: A bad reputation — one I try to change

indicators.note: change asks for these letters to be rearranged into something different

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a poor name resolving to reform themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges ONE, I, TRY and TO; the dash is punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy: being well known for something bad.

clue.text: Little Mary receives a prize (of sorts) for geometrical drawing

indicators.note: receives means the stomach word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Little Mary is old British slang for the stomach, as is tum

indicators.note: of sorts suggests a version of the words, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl called Mary winning a sort of award for a geometry diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' looks like a child but is old British slang for the stomach; 'of sorts' rearranges the prize letters, which 'receives' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with one pair of parallel sides, or none, depending on the convention.

clue.text: As a rule, it's good being in control

indicators.note: being in says the abbreviation goes inside the control word

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, so reins mean control

explanation.surface: A general maxim that it is beneficial to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a' and 'it's' are link words; 'rule' is the noun, meaning a monarch's period of sovereignty.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's time on the throne is their period of sovereignty.

clue.text: Character one employed in post

definitions.meaning: ... means distinctive character, as in a person of a different ...
a postage ... is used when sending mail by post

explanation.surface: A colourful person who has a job at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp means distinguishing mark or kind, and a postage label is stuck on letters sent through the mail.

clue.text: Bill given admission, finally, by the back door

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of admission

explanation.surface: A bill presented at the rear entrance after someone has been let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'by the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secondary gate or rear entrance, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Flier has to move slowly behind anti-radar device

indicators.note: behind places the slow-moving word after the radar decoy in the answer

parts.note: chaff is strips of foil dropped by aircraft to confuse radar
to inch is to move forward a little at a time

explanation.surface: An aircraft crawling along after releasing its radar countermeasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an airman, given the radar, but it is a bird. 'has' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch, a small songbird that flies.

clue.text: Suitable accommodation for fish? That's fine

indicators.note: accommodation for means the suitable word houses the fish inside it

parts.note: fit means suitable
the orfe is a freshwater fish, a kind of ide

explanation.surface: Asking whether a home is right for fish, and declaring it acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like approval but is a penalty. 'That's' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty paid for wrongdoing is a sum lost as punishment.

clue.text: Ore that's processed — it provides variable resistance

indicators.note: ore is processed in a refinery, so here the letters go through a reshaping

parts.note: taken as written
the contraction gives its letters as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Ore being treated, as a component in an electrical circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical component whose resistance can be adjusted, such as a dimmer control.

clue.text: Quick to put words in someone's mouth

definitions.text: to put words in someone's mouth
definitions.meaning: to ... an actor is to supply forgotten lines

explanation.surface: Someone eager to supply what others should say.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt as an adjective means speedy; as a verb it means feeding an actor their forgotten lines.

clue.text: Girl seen on the moon

definitions.meaning: the dark plains on the lunar surface, once thought to be seas

explanation.surface: A girl spotted on the lunar surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, and the Latin plural of mare, for the dark lowland seas visible on the lunar face.

clue.text: Security man

definitions.meaning: something left as security for a loan
a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A security guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods pledged against a loan, and the lowliest chess piece.

clue.text: Make one run — it entertains a bit

indicators.note: a bit says only a portion of these words is wanted, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Joining forces to keep something going that amuses people slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in rUN IT Entertains; the dash is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To join together into a single whole is to merge or combine.

clue.text: Man in field taking interest in county's comeback

indicators.note: taking means the reversed county holds the concern word inside it
comeback signals the county abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation of Worcestershire, an English county
care means concern or interest

explanation.surface: A farmer from the shires taking an interest in a local revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns WORCS into SCROW, which takes in CARE. Worcestershire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw-stuffed figure dressed in old clothes stands in crops to frighten birds.

clue.text: Religious type of West Indian

definitions.meaning: a religious, as a noun, is a monk or friar; a Black Friar of St Dominic's order
a native of the Caribbean island nation of Dominica or the ... Republic

explanation.surface: Describing a churchgoing person from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar of the order founded by St Dominic, or a citizen of a Caribbean republic.

clue.text: Fish that rise above water lose their heads

indicators.note: their heads takes the opening letter of each of the words just before

explanation.surface: Fish leaping out of the water are decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose' looks like a deletion signal, but it is just the last of the words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To fish with a large dragged net from a boat.
